text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:

-- Istvan Szent-Ivanyi, parliementary leader of the junior ruling coalition member the Free Democrats, said Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn and his Slovak counterpart Vladimir Meciar should not meet again until at least some of the controversial issues discussed by them last week are resolved.

-- A Slovak paper criticised Hungary for claiming more rights for the Hungarian ethnic minority in Slovakia. The paper called Hungary's foreign policy "expansive" and deemed the claims of the ethnic Hungarian unjustified.

-- The opposition party Hungarian Democrats (MDF) said it had collected 10,000 signatures supporting a referendum on the new law on land, which the MDF said would allow foreigners to buy land in Hungary.
-- The new self-government of the social security health care fund is likely to be set up today despite the withdrawal of Peter Simsa, the current vice-president, as a candidate.
